text:
maria: hit a nasty one — async client sometimes replays requests after a timeout and server double-applies writes. Repro steps below, has minimal logs

ajay: ow, thanks for flagging. Is this the AsyncClient or the sync Client? Any chance you set idempotency_key?

maria: AsyncClient. I wasn't setting idempotency_key for our internal create call. We generally relied on client retry logic + server dedupe but that didn't help here.

doris: can you paste the snippet that reproduces it? :eyes:

maria: yep — small repro
```python
from redwood import AsyncClient

async def create_item():
    async with AsyncClient(api_key=\"x...\") as c:
        # intentionally small timeout to trigger client-level timeout
        return await c.post(\"/items\", json={\"name\": \"replay-test\"}, timeout=1.0)
```

maria: sometimes this yields duplicate items. server logs show two distinct create events 500ms apart.

ajay: are you running with default retry/backoff settings? The client will retry on some transient errors but timeouts are tricky — it may have already sent the request but timed out waiting, then retrys and server treats as new.

maria: default AsyncClient(retries=3) — I didn't set idempotency_key. Behavior looked nondeterministic.

ci-bot: test run: test_async_replay (maria/repro) — failed 2/5, produced 2 items instead of 1

lee: server does dedupe by idempotency header only. If none, it's best-effort and depends on request body + timing; not guaranteed.

 d\oris: if we don't want callers changing code, maybe SDK should auto-attach an idempotency key for POST-like operations when a retry is enabled? But that breaks semantic if user expects non-idempotent behavior.

ajay: idea: SDK could auto-generate an idempotency-key for retries but only when it can safely replay (e.g., content-length small, no multipart). Also expose a `idempotency_strategy` flag: \"none\" | \"auto\" | \"explicit\".

maria: +1. Also: typing problem — AsyncClient.post signature currently typed as returning Dict[str, Any] but in async version type stubs are missing, mypy screams.

lee: aha — two issues then: 1) UX for idempotency + replay, 2) broken/absent typing for async APIs.

ajay: quick fix plan: add opt-in `auto_idempotency=true` for 1.1.2 patch; default remains off to preserve current semantics. Add consistent typed overloads for async/sync methods in stubs. Also add jittered exponential backoff for timeouts and retry_on_timeout flag.

 d\oris: we should document the server-side expectations in the SDK docs: how server dedupe works, what headers to set. Also include recommended pattern for create flows.

maria: workaround for now: add explicit idempotency key in header and bump timeout. Example
```python
await c.post(\"/items\", json=payload, headers={\"Idempotency-Key\": uuid4().hex}, timeout=5.0)
```

ajay: follow-up tasks:
- create SDK PR: auto_idempotency opt-in + idempotency_strategy enum (ajay)
- add types for async client and generate stubs (lee)
- doc blurb + quickstart note about retries/timeouts (doris)
- add e2e test that asserts no duplicate creates with auto_idempotency on (maria)

maria: thanks — i'll open the repro as an issue and add the failing CI run link. Filing now.

ci-bot: issue created: https://redwood/issue/INF-4321 — attached logs and minimal repro ✅

lee: quick question for design — if we auto-generate idempotency keys, should we persist them per-request (in-memory) across retries only, or cache them for some time so replays across process restarts can be deduped?

ajay: don't cache across restarts — that changes application semantics. Keep per-request only. Server-side dedupe TTL handles late duplicates.

doris: ok will update the design doc and mention TTL assumptions in the notes.

maria: one last note — observed error payload when dupe happened:

```
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
X-Request-ID: abc
{\"id\": \"item_123\"}

then later
HTTP/1.1 201 Created
{\"id\": \"item_124\"}
```

maria: weird that first returned 200 then 201, seems like one request timed out mid-response? maybe the client didn't receive the body.

ajay: yes that's consistent with socket read timeout: server committed create and returned, but client gave up waiting and retried. That combo is why idempotency is needed.

doris: assigning tasks and will track in INF-4321. Thanks for the detailed repro and logs, very actionable. :tada:
